analysis: The batch is documentation and changelog only: changelog.d/serving-stalls.md (new) and docs/architecture/hardware-support.md (mermaid load-gate edges at head lines 224-225, and a new paragraph at head lines 264-271). No executable code, auth, attestation, encryption, or wire-protocol change is visible, and the docs make no claim that changes TB-002/TB-011 receipt, authorization or attestation behavior. The changelog describes provider-side runtime behavior that the next pass should check in the actual code. (1) Paged KV pools retain free 64 MiB segments across requests, up to 1/8 of the slot grant and at most 2 GiB, and reinstall them for the next admission 'instead of allocating, zero-filling'. If a retained segment is reinstalled without clearing, a later request could read a prior consumer's KV bytes. That would touch T-028, residual inference data in GPU memory, and A-001. The paged-KV read path normally writes before it reads, but this is not shown here. The reviewer should verify that reinstall either zeroes the segment or that kernels never read unwritten slots. (2) Retained segments are 'uncommitted (no grant, floor or ledger charge)'. This was not confirmed against ProcessMemoryLedger or the memory-cap invariants in the doc: the cap invariant is 'Σ resident weights + KV + activations ≤ hardCapBytes', and the docs say retained segments are counted as reclaimable for load admission and are dropped on any refused charge or on memory pressure. Whether the uncommitted memory can cause OOM or denial of service (T-016/T-029 class) is therefore unverified. (3) Retention is bounded by a 30 s idle timeout, which narrows the residual-data window, but whether the segments are released on model unload, unlike the 'prefix cache', is not visible. (4) The new DARKBLOOM_TTFT_* env rollbacks are forwarded by `darkbloom start` to launchd-managed providers. The environment-injection surface is operator-local, with no new privilege. No threat-model mapping is claimed for the host-zero-fill-on-demand pages. No finding is raised because no code is in evidence; the actual implementation (CBv2RetainedKVSegments, KVPoolReclaimer, the paged pool) should be reviewed.
